text.en:
Now you ask where someone is.
¿Estás en casa? = Are you at home?
The words are the same as in “You are at home”.
A ¿ opens the question. A ? closes it.
In English, “are” jumps to the front. In Spanish, the words stay.
Your voice goes up at the end.

With a name, you can start with the changing word.
¿Está Ana en casa? = Is Ana at home?
Or you can keep the name first.
¿Ana está en la cocina? = Is Ana in the kitchen?
La cocina means “the kitchen”.
¿Están Ana y Luis en casa? = Are Ana and Luis at home?

Next you pick the right question.
Look at the ¿ ? marks. Then see who it is about.
¿Estamos cerca? = Are we nearby?
¿Está el pasaporte en la mochila? = Is the passport in the backpack?
El pasaporte means “the passport”. La mochila means “the backpack”.
¿Están los billetes en el bolso? = Are the tickets in the bag?
Los billetes means “the tickets”. El bolso means “the bag”.
